_why: Every modification this build makes to the PREBUILT ciel PDK volume, declared.
The Dockerfile asserts which open_pdks commit the volume was cut from by
resolving /foss/pdks/<fam> and requiring the sha in the resolved PATH. That
assertion is about PROVENANCE and is blind to CONTENT: a step that rewrites a
file inside the resolved tree leaves the path alone, so the assertion keeps
passing while the sentence it stands for stops being true.
tools/pdk/pdk_local_mods.py digests the volume before the first local step and
again after the last, and requires every measured difference to be covered by
an entry below. Adding a patch step without adding an entry FAILS THE BUILD
naming the undeclared files -- declaring is not something anyone has to
remember, it is the only way to get a green build. The expect_* counts fail in
both directions, so an entry cannot outlive the step it describes either.
Paths are relative to 'root'. `*` matches one path segment, `**` any depth --
the version segment is a `*` on purpose, so the sha lives in exactly one place
(the Dockerfile ARG) and this file does not have to be advanced with it.

modifications.what: sky130 HD and HVL tech LEFs: the five M4M5 vias carried a met5 patch of 1.42um on a layer whose own declared WIDTH is 1.6um, so a route terminating on one reports m5.1. The patch is grown to the layer's own minimum and the matching VIARULE GENERATE enclosure from 0.31 to 0.40. Upstream bytes, not ciel's; the volume is the only place that owns them.
modifications.scope_note: met5 only. The same contradiction exists on gf180's Metal2/Metal3/Metal5 (8 vias) on far denser layers whose DRC consequences have NOT been measured. Those files are deliberately absent from 'paths', so sweeping them in would fail this check rather than ride along.

modifications.issue: no tracker issue; docs/DEFECT_gf180mcu_pl8_poly_dummy_density.md — fixed UPSTREAM at globalfoundries-pdk-libs-gf180mcu_fd_pv 2404d27b583b (2026-07-04), which this prebuilt volume predates
modifications.what: gf180mcuD KLayout deck: PL.8 (poly2 density) counted layer 30/0 alone while the same PDK's tech/scripts/fill_poly2.rb writes its dummy poly on 30/4, so a die meeting the 14% floor WITH the fill this PDK generated was reported as violating it. The metal rules in the same file already union metal_drawn + metal_dummy. A derived layer :poly2_result = :poly2 + :poly2_dummy is registered in generic_layers.rb and PL.8 reads it. :poly2 itself is NOT redefined: DPF.5 is poly2_dummy.separation(poly2, 5um) and device extraction is poly2.and(comp), so the union arrives under a new name whose only consumer is the density rule.
modifications.scope_note: PL.8 only. Upstream's own fix (2404d27b583b) instead RENAMES 30/0 to :poly2_drawn and gives the union the name :poly2, which also hands the union to every rule that still says bare poly2 -- geom.rb's off-grid check, guard_ring.rb and others -- across 28 files. Those verdict changes are NOT measured here, so they are left to advancing the PDK volume rather than hand-ported into a binary artefact. The anchors are exact whole lines and the step declares --expect 2, so on a volume that already carries the upstream fix this step FAILS the build instead of applying somewhere else.

modifications.what: gf180mcuD klayout tech: the volume ships libs.tech/klayout/tech/scripts/sealring.py, whose first act is to put libs.tech/klayout/tech/pymacros on sys.path and do `from sealring_cells import gf180mcu_sealring` -- and that package is not in the volume, so the script prints "Error: Couldn't load the seal ring library." and exits 0. No ring is drawn and the die reaches tapeout_precheck unsealed, which is what turned General.SealRing from NOT_DETERMINED into FAIL. This step installs the four-file package from the SAME upstream commit whose copy of scripts/sealring.py is byte-identical to the one the volume already carries (fossi-foundation/globalfoundries-pdk-libs-gf180mcu_fd_pr e11a8c98dfc9, sha256 84cfcb8e2d5cacb018af11856fe8df07f77f10a5b27a476247d5e2599f800ece); see tools/pdk/sealring_cells/PROVENANCE.md.
modifications.scope_note: gf180mcuD only, and ADDITIVE only: four .py files into a directory that does not exist in the delivered volume. Nothing upstream delivered is modified, hence expect_modified 0. The step refuses to run if the destination already exists, so on a volume that grows its own copy this FAILS the build rather than silently overwriting it. The two ihp families' seal ring is a registered KLayout library (SG13_dev) and was blocked by an unrelated gap this entry does NOT sweep in: the PyCell runtime the PDK's own bootstrap imports was an empty submodule directory (vibeic-eda#173). That is installed by pdk_ihp_pycell_runtime_install.py in Dockerfile.derived 2/5, which has no entry here because the ihp trees are not under this manifest's ciel root; its own --expect count and pdk_pycell_lib_check.py are the tripwire for it.

modifications.what: gf180mcuD KLayout deck: CUP.2/CUP.3 (minimum width / space of the metal line used for bond pads) took the WHOLE layout's metal as their subject, so the foundry IO library's own qualified bond-pad metal -- 0.3um slots on a 2um pitch inside each cell's own Pad (37/0) opening -- was reported against itself. Every pad-bearing gf180mcu_fd_io master, checked ALONE exactly as the PDK ships it, reported 87 CUP.3; a die inherits 87 per bond pad (measured 38 pads -> 3306 flat / 7 masters -> 609 deep) with the design's fill, PDN, pad ring and seal ring contributing 0. rule_decks/cup.rb now extracts its subject with those masters, and everything under them, left unvisited (CUP_IO_PAD_MASTER_CELLS = 'gf180mcu_fd_io__*', applied to a RecursiveShapeIterator over the deck's own layout -- NOT a second DRC source, which is a second deep shape store and kills every connectivity rule in the deck under decks=all). The Pad and GUARD_RING_MK layers are NOT filtered, so design metal reaching into a foundry cell's bond-pad opening -- the literal circuit-under-pad -- is still the subject and is still checked.
modifications.scope_note: CUP.2/CUP.3 only, and by CELL MASTER because no marker exists: every marker layer the IO library carries (lvs_io 119/5, esd_mk 24/5, latchup_mk 137/5, ...) lies above y=68.7um in gf180mcu_fd_io__bi_t while its Pad opening is y=2..62um, so nothing the PDK draws marks that metal. The deck's only existing escape, not_interacting(guard_ring_mk), is the guard-ring STRUCTURE marker: stamping 167/5 over one bond pad was measured to remove 87 CUP.3 and add 762 GR.1/GR.2/GR.4. NOT fixed upstream -- globalfoundries-pdk-libs-gf180mcu_fd_pv at 035e6d1f ships cup.rb byte-identical to the volume's copy (md5 6a4e724731d04b657f9a96e73e45256b), so unlike the PL.8 entry above, advancing the PDK volume would NOT bring a fix. Both directions are run through the deck itself at build time by tools/pdk/pdk_gf180_cup_check.py, which returns rc=1 on the deck as shipped. The anchors are exact whole lines and the step declares --expect 2, so on a deck that has moved this FAILS the build instead of applying somewhere else.

modifications.issue: vibe-ic F22 (step 30 SPICE/STA correlation, lane migf22)
modifications.what: gf180mcuD Xyce models: every transistor of the 5 V standard-cell libraries is a call of nfet_05v0 / pfet_05v0 (gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0.spice: 2403 + 2405 calls). The ngspice tree of the same volume defines both in its fets_mm section as the statistical wrapper of the 6 V model with the 5 V defaults; the Xyce tree defines neither -- a .subckt census of the two trees differs by exactly these two names -- so no 5 V standard cell simulates in Xyce (Xyce 7.10 on 0.3.79: 'Subcircuit NFET_05V0 has not been defined for instance X_I_1'; vibe-ic step 30's Xyce arm refused LL_SPICE_DEVICE_UNMODELLED on 0.3.79). The step copies the Xyce tree's OWN nfet_06v0 / pfet_06v0 wrapper under the 05v0 name with the defaults the ngspice definition declares, inserted before it in the same .lib section, and refuses when the two wrappers' statistical parameters differ. MEASURED after the patch, spm register-to-register path at max_ss_125C_4v50 with layout-extracted cells: Xyce 10.023 ns vs ngspice 10.026 ns.
modifications.scope_note: gf180mcuD Xyce model tree only, ADDITIVE inside two existing files: two .subckt blocks each into sm141064.xyce and its byte-identical twin sm141064.spice. No existing line changes, the ngspice tree is untouched, and the step refuses if either name is already defined, so a volume that ships them FAILS the build rather than defining them twice.
